screening_decisions.reason: Randomised controlled trial in women with urinary stress incontinence. Two intervention arms involved pelvic floor muscle exercises (with or without biofeedback) and a third arm received no exercises. Meets all selection criteria.

Randomised controlled trial in women with stress urinary incontinence. The intervention arm used a mobile app treatment focused on pelvic floor muscle training; the control arm had postponed treatment (no active intervention during the study period). Meets design, population and comparison criteria.

Randomised controlled trial in postmenopausal women with stress urinary incontinence comparing pelvic floor muscle exercises alone, pelvic floor exercises plus biofeedback, and a control group that was assessed but did not receive treatment sessions. Contains a PFMT arm and a no-treatment control arm.

Randomised placebo-controlled trial in older women with urge or mixed urinary incontinence. One arm received biofeedback-assisted behavioural treatment, which in this context teaches pelvic floor muscle control; another arm was a placebo control condition. Meets criteria, though the explicit mention of pelvic floor muscles is indirect.

Randomised controlled trial in older community-dwelling women with sphincteric incompetence (stress incontinence). Arms included biofeedback, pelvic muscle exercise, and a control group. Contains a PFMT arm and a no-treatment control arm.

Single-blind randomised controlled trial in women with genuine stress incontinence. Arms were pelvic floor exercises, electrical stimulation, vaginal cones, and an untreated control group. The PFMT arm versus no-treatment comparison satisfies the selection criteria.

Experimental study with random allocation of women with stress urinary incontinence to a pelvic floor exercise group or a control group. The control group served as comparator without active intervention. Meets criteria, although the abstract is brief on control details.

Single-blind randomised controlled trial in women with urodynamic stress urinary incontinence comparing pelvic floor muscle training, electrical stimulation, vaginal cones, and an untreated control group. A PFMT versus no-treatment comparison is present.

Prospective randomised controlled clinical trial in women with stress and mixed urinary incontinence. Participants were allocated to a pelvic floor muscle training group or a control group with no exercise program. Meets all criteria.

Randomised controlled trial in women with urinary incontinence. The treatment group received a behavioural modification program that produced measurable improvements in pelvic floor muscle strength, indicating PFMT content; the control group had no treatment. Meets criteria.

Prospective randomised study comparing two active physical therapies (medical gymnastics and perineal electrical stimulation) for genuine stress incontinence. No no-treatment, placebo, sham or inactive control arm is described. Fails the comparison criterion.

Randomised controlled trial (described as crossover) in elderly women with stress urinary incontinence. An intervention group received exercises aimed at enhancing pelvic floor muscles and fitness; a control group was used for comparison. The design includes a PFMT arm and an inactive comparator.

Randomised controlled trial in elderly women with stress, urge and mixed urinary incontinence. Exercise groups received training that included pelvic floor muscle work; an education group served as an inactive control. Meets the PFMT versus inactive control requirement.

Randomised controlled trial in elderly women with stress, urge and mixed urinary incontinence. The intervention group received multidimensional exercise treatment including pelvic floor muscle training; the control group had no active treatment. Meets criteria.

Controlled trial with random assignment in older women with mild-to-moderate urinary incontinence. The intervention included pelvic floor muscle training with manual palpation/verbal feedback and behavioural therapy; the control group received only advice and an educational pamphlet (inactive control).

Randomised controlled trial in women with stress urinary incontinence. The treatment group received physiotherapist-supervised pelvic floor muscle training; the control group received no treatment. Directly meets all criteria.

Prospective randomised single-blind interventional study in women with mild stress urinary incontinence. The immediate intervention group was taught a pelvic floor muscle precontraction skill; the wait-listed control group acted as a no-treatment comparator during the initial study period.

Randomised controlled pilot study in women with stress urinary incontinence. Groups were individual PFMT, group PFMT, and a control group that received no treatment during the study period. Meets all criteria.

Pilot randomised controlled trial in women with mixed urinary incontinence. Arms were traditional Chinese medicine acupuncture, pelvic floor muscle training, and a waiting-list control. Contains a PFMT arm and an inactive control arm.

Single parallel-group randomised controlled trial in postmenopausal women with urinary incontinence. The physical therapy for UI arm would standardly include pelvic floor muscle training; the control arm received osteoporosis education, which is an inactive control for UI. Meets criteria.

Randomised controlled trial comparing bladder training, pelvic muscle exercises, and a control group in women with urinary incontinence. The pelvic muscle exercise arm and the control arm satisfy the PFMT versus no-treatment comparison.

Experimental randomised study in women with stress urinary incontinence. Participants were divided into kinesitherapy groups (including pelvic floor muscle work) and a control group that showed no significant change. Meets criteria.

Experimental randomised study in female volleyball athletes with stress urinary incontinence. The experimental group underwent a pelvic floor muscle rehabilitation program; the control group had access to a pamphlet only (inactive). Meets criteria.

Randomised controlled trial in women with genuine stress incontinence. Arms included pelvic floor exercises, interferential therapy, oestrogen, and a control group that showed no significant change. PFMT versus no-treatment comparison is present.

Controlled randomised trial in women with urinary stress incontinence in general practice. The treatment group received pelvic floor exercise instruction; the control group received no therapy. Meets all criteria.

Parallel-group randomised clinical trial in women with stress or mixed urinary incontinence. Participants were assigned to pelvic floor muscle training or an untreated control group with no contact during the intervention period. Meets all criteria.

This article describes the protocol of a pragmatic randomised controlled trial. It is not a report of a completed trial with results, and therefore does not meet the requirement for a randomised controlled trial report at this screening stage.

Secondary analysis of an RCT focusing on consumer satisfaction with nurse-led versus GP-led care for urinary incontinence. The intervention is a care delivery model rather than explicit pelvic floor muscle training, the control is usual GP care of uncertain activity, and the abstract does not report UI outcomes. Does not clearly meet the PFMT versus inactive control criterion.

Randomised controlled trial in older women with urge or mixed urinary incontinence. Arms included biofeedback-assisted behavioural training, behavioural training without biofeedback (verbal feedback based on vaginal palpation), and a self-help booklet control. The behavioural training arms teach pelvic floor muscle control, providing a PFMT versus inactive control comparison.

Feasibility study in which women volunteered for a pelvic floor fitness program. There was no randomisation to a no-treatment or inactive control arm in a controlled trial design. Fails the design criterion.

Randomised comparative trial in women with stress urinary incontinence comparing intensive supervised PFMT with unsupervised PFMT. Both arms received active pelvic floor muscle training; there was no no-treatment, placebo or inactive control arm. Fails the comparison criterion.

Randomised clinical trial in women with chronic low back pain and stress urinary incontinence comparing stabilisation exercises focusing on pelvic floor muscles versus routine physiotherapy modalities and regular exercises. The control arm is an active treatment, not a no-treatment or inactive control. Fails the comparison criterion.

Randomised controlled trial in women with stress or mixed urinary incontinence comparing behavioural training, behavioural training plus pelvic floor electrical stimulation, and a self-help booklet control. Behavioural training for stress incontinence incorporates pelvic floor muscle training, providing a PFMT versus inactive control comparison.

Randomised controlled trial in elderly women with urinary incontinence residing in long-term care. The training program included Kegel’s exercises (pelvic floor muscle training); the control group did not receive the training program. Meets criteria.

Randomised controlled trial in women with urinary incontinence comparing behavioural therapy with a no-therapy control group. Behavioural therapy for UI conventionally includes pelvic floor muscle training, and the control is inactive. Meets criteria.

Economic evaluation conducted alongside an RCT that compared two modes of delivering pelvic floor muscle training (Internet-based versus postal). The trial did not include an actual no-treatment, placebo, sham or inactive control arm; the no-treatment comparator was modelled hypothetically. Fails the comparison criterion.

Randomised controlled study comparing Internet-based pelvic floor muscle training with a postal program for stress urinary incontinence. There was no no-treatment, placebo, sham or other inactive control treatment arm. Fails the comparison criterion.

Follow-up report of the same RCT as study 37 comparing Internet-based versus postal pelvic floor muscle training. No no-treatment or inactive control arm was included in the trial. Fails the comparison criterion.

Randomised controlled trial in women with stress urinary incontinence comparing transverse abdominal and pelvic floor muscle co-contraction exercises with a control group. The intervention is a form of PFMT and the control group received no treatment. Meets criteria.

Pilot randomised controlled trial in frail older women combining behavioural urinary incontinence treatments with general physical activity (walking and strength training). The intervention is not explicitly pelvic floor muscle training, and the abstract does not describe a clear no-treatment or inactive control. Does not clearly meet the PFMT versus inactive control criterion.

Randomised controlled trial in gynaecological cancer survivors with pelvic floor dysfunction. The population is not explicitly women with stress, urgency or mixed urinary incontinence based on symptoms/signs/urodynamics, and urinary incontinence outcomes are not described. Fails the population criterion.

Development and psychometric evaluation of the ICIQ questionnaire. This is a measurement study, not a randomised or quasi-randomised controlled trial of pelvic floor muscle training. Fails the design criterion.
Systematic review of randomised clinical trials on conservative treatment of stress urinary incontinence. This is a review, not a primary trial. Fails the design criterion.
Systematic review of randomised clinical trials on conservative treatment of urge urinary incontinence. This is a review, not a primary trial. Fails the design criterion.
Consensus statement extending CONSORT reporting guidelines for nonpharmacologic trials. This is a methodological guideline, not a trial. Fails the design criterion.
Narrative overview discussing the impact of urinary incontinence and general interventions. Not a randomised or quasi-randomised controlled trial. Fails the design criterion.
Cross-cultural psychometric validation of the I-QOL measure. Not a trial of pelvic floor muscle training. Fails the design criterion.
Reproducibility study of instruments for subjective evaluation of stress urinary incontinence. Not a randomised controlled trial. Fails the design criterion.
Imaging study using MRI to assess pelvic floor muscle function. Not a randomised controlled trial. Fails the design criterion.
Narrative review discussing theories behind why pelvic floor muscle training is effective. Not a primary trial. Fails the design criterion.
IUGA/ICS joint terminology report on conservative management of female pelvic floor dysfunction. Not a trial. Fails the design criterion.
Secondary analysis of a cross-sectional epidemiological survey (EpiLUTS). Not a randomised controlled trial. Fails the design criterion.
Pharmacology review of the lower urinary tract. Not a trial. Fails the design criterion.
Narrative review discussing optimal pelvic floor muscle training regimens. Not a primary trial. Fails the design criterion.
Clinical report on functional electrical stimulation for bladder inhibition. Not a randomised controlled trial of PFMT versus inactive control. Fails the design criterion.
Secondary analysis of pelvic muscle resting data in healthy women. Not a trial in women with urinary incontinence. Fails the population and design criteria.
GRADE guideline article on preparing summary of findings tables for binary outcomes. Not a trial. Fails the design criterion.
GRADE guideline article on preparing summary of findings tables for continuous outcomes. Not a trial. Fails the design criterion.
Community-based epidemiological survey (EPINCONT) of female urinary incontinence prevalence. Not a randomised controlled trial. Fails the design criterion.
IUGA/ICS joint terminology report on female pelvic floor dysfunction. Not a trial. Fails the design criterion.
Methodological note on analysis of quality of interventions in systematic reviews. Not a primary trial. Fails the design criterion.
Cross-sectional observational study measuring quality of life in women with urinary incontinence using the Sickness Impact Profile. Not a randomised controlled trial. Fails the design criterion.
Systematic review and economic modelling of non-surgical treatments for stress urinary incontinence. Not a primary trial. Fails the design criterion.
Development and psychometric testing of the Bristol Female Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms questionnaire. Not a trial. Fails the design criterion.
Willingness-to-pay study in patients with urge incontinence. Not a randomised controlled trial. Fails the design criterion.
Cross-sectional analysis of national survey data examining association of urinary incontinence with self-rated health. Not a randomised controlled trial. Fails the design criterion.
Development and validation of a condition-specific quality of life questionnaire for women with urinary incontinence. Not a trial. Fails the design criterion.

Instrument development and testing (YIPS) nested within a longitudinal randomised control study of a behavioural/educational intervention. The abstract reports only instrument psychometrics, not the trial outcomes, and the intervention is not explicitly pelvic floor muscle training. Fails to clearly meet the PFMT intervention criterion.
Content validity study of the King’s Health Questionnaire in patients with overactive bladder. Not a trial of pelvic floor muscle training. Fails the design criterion.
Methodological study examining whether quality of trial reports affects meta-analysis estimates. Not a primary trial. Fails the design criterion.
CONSORT statement revised recommendations for reporting parallel-group randomised trials. Not a trial. Fails the design criterion.
Follow-up survey assessing bothersomeness and quality of life impact of urinary incontinence in community-dwelling women. Not a randomised controlled trial. Fails the design criterion.

Observational study of pelvic muscle activity in healthy nulliparous volunteers. Population does not have urinary incontinence and it is not a controlled trial. Fails the population and design criteria.
Development and validation of a severity index for epidemiological surveys of female urinary incontinence. Not a trial. Fails the design criterion.
Cross-sectional study of female sexual function in women with urinary incontinence. Not a randomised controlled trial. Fails the design criterion.
Prospective cohort study testing responsiveness of the Geriatric Self-Efficacy Index for UI. Not a randomised controlled trial of PFMT. Fails the design criterion.
Development of short-form versions of the Incontinence Impact Questionnaire and Urogenital Distress Inventory. Not a trial. Fails the design criterion.
Development of the I-QOL quality of life measure for urinary incontinence. Not a trial. Fails the design criterion.
Validation of the Quality of Life Scale in Norwegian patients with psoriasis. Not related to urinary incontinence or pelvic floor muscle training. Fails the population and design criteria.
Validation of global impression questionnaires using data from drug trials. Not a trial of pelvic floor muscle training. Fails the design criterion.
Development of the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale. Not a trial of pelvic floor muscle training. Fails the design criterion.

Randomised controlled trial in obese perimenopausal women with stress urinary incontinence. The intervention group received supervised pelvic floor muscle exercise training; the control group served as comparator without the training program. Meets all criteria.

Randomised study in women with stress urinary incontinence comparing perineal exercises with and without electrotherapy against a control group. The exercise arms represent pelvic floor muscle training and the control group received no intervention. Meets criteria.

Randomised controlled trial of acupressure versus sham acupressure versus usual care for urodynamic stress incontinence. No arm involved pelvic floor muscle training as the intervention. Fails the intervention criterion.

Randomised trial comparing a supervised pelvic floor exercise program added to a conventional home exercise program versus the home program alone for stress urinary incontinence. Both arms included active pelvic floor muscle training; there was no no-treatment or inactive control arm. Fails the comparison criterion.

Randomised controlled trial in women with stress urinary incontinence with four arms: duloxetine alone, pelvic floor muscle training alone, combined treatment, and no active treatment. The PFMT alone versus no active treatment comparison meets all selection criteria.

Qualitative interview study exploring women’s experiences of Internet-based or postal treatment for stress urinary incontinence. Not a primary randomised controlled trial report of efficacy. Fails the design criterion.

Abstract reporting predictors of success from a non-face-to-face pelvic floor muscle training program. The underlying trial compared Internet-based versus postal delivery of PFMT without a no-treatment or inactive control arm. Fails the comparison criterion.

Systematic review protocol evaluating pelvic floor muscle training added to another active treatment versus the same active treatment alone. This is a review, not a primary trial. Fails the design criterion.
Exercise physiology perspective review on pelvic floor muscle exercise for stress urinary incontinence. Not a primary trial. Fails the design criterion.
Anatomical review of urethrovesical structure. Not a trial. Fails the design criterion.
Development and validation of the Hopkins Symptom Checklist. Not a trial of pelvic floor muscle training. Fails the design criterion.
Review chapter on adult conservative management of urinary incontinence and pelvic organ prolapse. Not a primary trial. Fails the design criterion.
Methodological article on post-randomisation exclusions and the intention-to-treat principle. Not a trial. Fails the design criterion.
Cochrane review protocol on pelvic floor muscle training versus other active treatments for urinary incontinence. This is a review, not a primary trial. Fails the design criterion.
Communication on outcome measures for lower urinary tract dysfunction research. Not a trial. Fails the design criterion.

Observational MRI cohort study nested within a quasi-experimental study. Not a randomised or quasi-randomised controlled trial with a PFMT versus inactive control comparison. Fails the design criterion.

Randomised controlled trial comparing conservative treatment (combined physiotherapy and bladder retraining) given without prior urodynamics versus the same conservative treatment tailored after urodynamics. Both arms received active treatment; there was no no-treatment or inactive control arm. Fails the comparison criterion.
Clinical and physiological observational study of pathophysiology of urinary incontinence in institutionalised elderly persons. Not a randomised controlled trial. Fails the design criterion.

Cochrane review on pelvic floor muscle training for prevention and treatment of urinary and faecal incontinence in antenatal and postnatal women. This is a review, not a primary trial. Fails the design criterion.
